name: Bipartite Matching and Linear Assignment
problem_statement: Given a bipartite graph, find a matching (a set of edges with no shared endpoints) that is optimal under a declared objective: maximum cardinality, maximum total weight, or minimum total cost.

normalization: Reject edges whose endpoints share the same declared side.
Reject self-loops (impossible in valid bipartite input).
Collapse parallel edges between the same pair by keeping the single best-objective weight.

problem_inputs.name: objective
problem_inputs.description: Maximize the number of matched pairs, maximize total matched weight, or minimize total matched cost.

problem_inputs.name: weight_mode
problem_inputs.description: maximum_cardinality always behaves as unweighted; maximum_weight and minimum_cost require edge_weight.

problem_inputs.name: perfect_matching_required
problem_inputs.description: Whether every vertex on the smaller side (or both sides, if equal size) must be covered by the returned matching; infeasibility must be reported explicitly rather than returning a partial match.

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: This problem is polynomial-time solvable; exact is the default, with approximate permitted only for very large instances with a disclosed bound.

required_outputs.name: matching_edges
required_outputs.description: Selected edges forming the matching; no two share a vertex.

required_outputs.name: matching_size
required_outputs.description: Number of matched pairs, equal to |matching_edges|.

required_outputs.name: objective_value
required_outputs.description: Total weight/cost of matching_edges under the declared objective (equal to matching_size for maximum_cardinality).

optional_outputs.name: unmatched_left_vertices
optional_outputs.description: Left-side vertices not covered by matching_edges.

optional_outputs.name: unmatched_right_vertices
optional_outputs.description: Right-side vertices not covered by matching_edges.

optional_outputs.name: feasible
optional_outputs.description: Whether a perfect matching exists, when perfect_matching_required=true.

optional_outputs.name: approximation_bound
optional_outputs.description: Certified relative error bound for an approximate result.

solution_semantics.objective: Select a matching optimal under the declared objective: maximize |matching_edges| for maximum_cardinality, maximize total weight for maximum_weight, or minimize total weight for minimum_cost.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exact mode requires optimal=true; this problem admits polynomial-time exact algorithms (augmenting paths, Hungarian algorithm), so approximate mode is only for extreme scale and must disclose approximation_bound.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each vertex appears in at most one entry of matching_edges.

validation_rules: matching_edges forms a valid matching (no two edges share an endpoint) in the normalized bipartite graph.
objective_value recomputes exactly as the sum of matched edge weights (or equals matching_size for maximum_cardinality).
perfect_matching_required=true with feasible=true implies every vertex on the smaller (or both, if equal) side is covered; feasible=false must correspond to a provably infeasible instance.
edge_cases: An edgeless graph has matching_size zero and empty matching_edges.
A graph admitting a perfect matching must return one when perfect_matching_required=true.
Maximum matching size is bounded above by the smaller side's vertex count.
Negative weights under minimum_cost are valid input and must not be clamped to zero.

correctness: optimality agreement with an exact oracle (e.g. Hopcroft-Karp or Hungarian algorithm) on small/medium fixtures
performance: augmenting paths or auction rounds performed
